html:
The Battle of Manila Bay was fought on 1 May 1898 in the bay off Manila in the Philippines. An American squadron under Commodore George Dewey destroyed the Spanish fleet in the Pacific in one morning.

It was the first big battle of the Spanish-American War, which began in April 1898 over Spanish rule in Cuba. The Philippines had been a colony of Spain for over 300 years, and Filipinos were already in revolt. Dewey sailed from Hong Kong with six modern warships and slipped into the bay at night. At dawn he found Admiral Patricio Montojo's older ships anchored off Cavite. The Americans steamed past them in a line, firing, several times. By noon every Spanish ship was sunk or burning. Spain counted 77 dead by its own figures. No American was killed in the fighting.

American troops took Manila in August. In the peace treaty Spain sold the Philippines to the United States for 20 million dollars. Filipinos who had expected independence fought the new rulers in the Philippine-American War. The battle made the United States a power in Asia and the Pacific. The Philippines became independent in 1946.
